Study: Asexual blood stages, salivary gland sporozoite and midgut oocyst transcriptomes (Gomez-Diaz) (RNA-seq)
Description: Description= Transcriptional analysis of asexual blood stages from 4 infected donors and the salivary gland sporozoites and midgut oocysts resulting from infecting mosquitoes with their blood. Sample generation: Mosquitoes were infected with blood from four independent malaria-affected donors. One donor carried only P. falciparum gametocytes, whereas the blood of the other donors carried both gametocytes and a large number of rings. (Only gametocytes are able to infect the mosquito.) In spite of the differences in the fraction of gametocytes present in the blood of the four donors, the percentage of infected mosquitoes and the mean number of oocyst found per midgut are very similar between infections. Samples analyzed: To determine the extent of transcriptional changes that P. falciparum may undergo during its life cycle in the mosquito, RNA-Seq analyses was carried out on blood samples from all four human donors. RNA-Seq was also performed on 7-day oocysts from the midgut of infected An. gambiae and 14-day sporozoites from their salivary glands obtained from infections #1 and #2.

Study: Dual transcriptomes of malaria-infected Gambian children (RNA-Seq)
Description: Description= Plasmodium portion of a dual RNA-Seq on whole blood, collected prior to treatment, from 46 Gambian children with P. falciparum uncomplicated malaria (n = 21) and severe malaria (n = 25). These children were recruited from a region with relatively low malaria transmission and consistent with this epidemiology, the severe malaria group contained children with cerebral malaria, hyperlactatemia, or a combination thereof, but no cases of severe anemia.These data are aligned to the Pf3D7 genome while the samples were sourced from individuals infected with naturally occurring parasites. Thus quantification based on alignment to the 3D7 genome should be interpreted with caution for polymorphic genes. The data presented in the publication was adjusted for variation in leukocyte subpopulation proportions and parasite developmental stage, therefore direct comparison with the data presented in PlasmoDB and HostDB is not possible.

Study: Intraerythrocytic development cycle transcriptome (2019) (Wichers et al. 2019) (RNA-seq)
Description: Description= The parasite Plasmodium falciparum is responsible for severe malaria, which is still one of the major causes of death in developing countries. This data provides an RNA-seq reference dataset for the Pf3D7 blood-stage transcriptome. A time course experiment with three independent biological replicates of synchronized 3D7 cells was performed. RNA-seq samples were taken at 8 developmental stages including young ring stage (8 hpi), late ring stage/early trophozoite (16 hpi), mid-age trophozoite (24 hpi), late trophozoite (32 hpi), early schizont (40 hpi), schizont (44 hpi), late schizont (48 hpi) and purified merozoites (0 hpi). Methodology used: RNA-seq time course experiment assayed by paired end, unstranded Illumina HiSeq 4000. Synchronized 3D7 parasites were used to generate a reference transcription profile. We performed 100-bp paired-end RNA-seq and generated an average of 11.7 (1.9) million paired-end reads per sample in biological triplicates. The generated sequence data set provides a deeper coverage of the blood-stage transcriptome than previously published RNA-seq studies. ArrayExpress E-MTAB-7731. Samples include: young ring stage [8 hpi], late ring stage/early trophozoite [16 hpi], mid-age trophozoite [24 hpi], late trophozoite [32 hpi], early schizont [40 hpi], schizont [44 hpi], late schizont [48 hpi], purified merozoites [0 hpi]

Intraerythrocytic development cycle transcriptome by DAFT-Seq (3D7, HB3, IT, 2020) (Chappell et al. 2020) (RNA-seq)
Description: Description= Directional, amplification-free RNA-seq protocol (DAFT-seq) records more complete sequence coverage which produces more accurate measures of gene expression than traditional PCR based RNA-Seq techniques. DAFT-seq was used to determine the transcriptome during the intraerythrocytic development cycles (IDCs) of three strains of P. falciparum: 3D7 (the genome reference strain, and presumed to be of West African origin), HB3 (a drug sensitive isolate from Honduras) and IT (widely used for studies of antigenic variation). Analysis of the resulting DAFT-seq data revealed extensive transcription between coding regions, particularly of long and often overlapping UTRs. Methodology used:directional, amplification-free RNA-seq protocol (DAFT-seq)

Study: Oocyst and salivary gland sporozoite transcriptome comparison in P. falciparum (Lindner et al.) (RNA-seq)
Description: Description= Sporozoite - oocyst transcriptome comparison. As the sporozoite transitions through the hemocoel from the oocyst to the salivary glands, the sporozoite undergoes a transition from being weakly infectious to highly infectious for the mammalian host. A comparison of the sporozoite and oocyst transcriptomes sheads light on the factors that change with increased infectiousness. By leveraging RNA-seq and greatly improved sporozoite purification strategies, this data set represents a more comprehensive transcriptome of sporozoites from human-infectious P. falciparum species. This data has associated P yoelii transcriptomic data as well as P falciparum and P yoelii proteomic data. Methodology used: Barcoded libraries were created using the Illumina TruSeq Stranded mRNA Library Prep Kit, according to the manufacturerâ€™s protocol. Sequencing was conducted on an Illumina HiSeq 2500 using 100 nt single read length on three biological replicates per sample type.

Study: Polysomal and steady-state asexual stage transcriptomes (Bunnik et al.) (RNA-seq)
Description: Description= Analysis of the levels of steady-state mRNA and polysome-associated mRNA at the ring, trophozoite, and schizont stages of the intra-erythrocytic cycle of P. falciparum 3D7 using Illumina sequencing.For steady-state mRNA, total RNA was isolated followed by mRNA purification using poly-A selection. For the same time points, polysomes were isolated by sucrose density gradient centrifugation, also followed by mRNA purification using poly-A selection. mRNA was converted to double-stranded DNA. Library preparations for steady-state mRNA samples were performed using the NuGEN Encore Multiplexing System, while library preparations for polysomal mRNA samples were performed using the New England Biolabs NEBNext ChIP-Seq Library Preparation kit. For all library preparations, PCR amplifications were performed using KAPA HiFi HotStart Ready Mix.

Trophozoite and Schizont transcriptomes of PfBDP1HA (Josling et al 2015) (RNA-seq)
Description: Description= During red-blood-cell-stage infection of Plasmodium falciparum, the parasite undergoes repeated rounds of replication, egress, and invasion. Erythrocyte invasion involves specific interactions between host cell receptors and parasite ligands and coordinated expression of genes specific to this step of the life cycle. We show that a parasite-specific bromodomain protein, PfBDP1, binds to chromatin at transcriptional start sites of invasion-related genes and directly controls their expression. Conditional PfBDP1 knockdown causes a dramatic defect in parasite invasion and growth and results in transcriptional downregulation of multiple invasion-related genes at a time point critical for invasion. Conversely, PfBDP1 overexpression enhances expression of these same invasion-related genes. PfBDP1 binds to acetylated histone H3 and a second bromodomain protein, PfBDP2, suggesting a potential mechanism for gene recognition and control. Collectively, these findings show that PfBDP1 critically coordinates expression of invasion genes and indicate that targeting PfBDP1 could be an invaluable tool in malaria eradication.
